A relic is a record in Workbook beside tasks. It holds specs, plans, decisions and similar material as named parts, with the same history and sharing that tasks have.

This is a follow-up from the review of the first six relics stories (finding M66). It was left out of that work on purpose.

## Problem

When a relic's ref moves, the index reads the changes it has not seen. To find them it asks Git for the parent of every commit in that relic's history (`git rev-list --parents`, in `relicParentGraph`), and then reads only the commits after the last one it indexed. So the listing grows with the relic's whole history, while the reading does not. Tasks do the same in `parentGraphFor`.

Nothing measures this. The benchmark gives every task the same short history, and no scenario changes one relic or one task that has a long history.

## Wanted

- Measure the cost of one change to a relic with a long history, and to a task with a long history.
- End the listing at the last indexed commit, for relics and for tasks, so a change costs the same whatever the length of the history. Walking the whole history on every change is not needed even where it is cheap.
- Keep the full walk for the cases that need it: the first index of a record, and a ref that no longer descends from the last indexed commit (a replay, or a compacted task).

## Done when

- The benchmark has a scenario that changes a relic with at least 1,000 commits, and one that changes a task with at least 1,000 commits. Each reports time and what Git was asked to list.
- After the change, the number of commits Git lists for one new change does not grow with the history, for relics and for tasks.
- A ref that does not descend from the last indexed commit is still indexed in full, with a test for a relic and a test for a task.

## Notes

Dylan asked on 2026-11-26 for the task measurement and for the walk to stop at the last indexed commit in both.
End the history listing at the last indexed commit, for relics and tasks
